name: Citizenship by Descent (Jus Sanguinis)

qualifying_event.description: A child born to at least one Greek-citizen parent acquires Greek citizenship automatically at birth (Article 1.1), regardless of where the birth takes place.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Foreign birth certificate; Greek parent's citizenship documentation; civil registry declaration.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires at least one parent to be a Greek citizen at the time of the child's birth. Acquisition is automatic and does not require residence in Greece.

sources.title: Greek Ministry of Foreign Affairs -- Codification of Legislation, Article 1.1 (automatic citizenship acquisition by descent at birth)
GLOBALCIT -- Greek Citizenship Code (as of 2010), Article 1.1 and Article 11 (foreign-born children of Greek-origin parents through parental naturalisation)

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Greece's initial build. Article 1.1 (automatic citizenship for a child of a Greek-citizen parent) confirmed independently at BOTH tier-1 (MFA codification) and tier-2 (GLOBALCIT) -- unusually well corroborated for this dataset. A separate mechanism exists (Article 11) for foreign-born children of Greek-ORIGIN (not necessarily citizen) parents to acquire citizenship automatically as minors when the parent naturalises -- not modelled as its own route here since it is a derivative effect of the parent's own naturalisation (gr_naturalisation) rather than an independently reachable route for the child themselves.
